feedback.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(\mu ,{7}^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-3\mu <X<5\mu )=0.6476,$ use the table to determine $\mu ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ | $\,0.7967\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ | $\,0.8238\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-3\mu <X<5\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$*

$\mu ≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Note that we can write the given probability as

$$
P(\mu -4\mu <X<\mu +4\mu )=0.6476,
$$

which tells us that the interval $-3\mu <X<5\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$

First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mu -4\mu <X<\mu +4\mu ) & =0.6476 \\ 2P(\mu <X<\mu +4\mu ) & =0.6476 \\ P(\mu <X<\mu +4\mu ) & =0.3238 \\ P(X<\mu +4\mu )-P(X<\mu ) & =0.3238 \\ P(X<\mu +4\mu )-0.5 & =0.3238 \\ P(X<\mu +4\mu ) & =0.8238 \\ P(X\le \mu +4\mu ) & =0.8238 \\ P(X\le 5\mu ) & =0.8238\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5\mu ) & =0.8238 \\ P(Z\le \frac{5\mu -\mu }{7}) & =0.8238 \\ Φ(\frac{4\mu }{7}) & =0.8238 \\ \frac{4\mu }{7} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8238)\end{aligned}
$$

 

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.93)=0.8238\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.8238)=0.93.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\mu }{7} & =0.93 \\ 4\mu  & =6.51 \\ \mu  & =\frac{6.51}{4} \\ \mu  & ≈1.63.\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
